report.summary: Reviewed daedalus/council/bus.py chunk 3 of 3 (lines 561-end): append_round, append_turn, append_roster, load_transcript, transcript_head, read_anchor, verify_chain. Claims mostly kept; one docstring claim uncheckable against this chunk.
risks: append_round | medium | Docstring says 'Turns are normalised, secret-floored, then sorted by actor id and chained with seq assigned here' but this chunk does not contain the _normalize_turn or secret_floor_rule application visible; the claim is only partially checkable here. What would settle it: inspect _normalize_turn and _scan_turn in earlier chunks.

append_roster | medium | Docstring says 'Counts are DERIVED here, never accepted from the caller' — observed that counts are computed from norm, but the participant dicts themselves come from the caller and fields like 'vendor' and 'model' are derived with fallbacks; the claim about counts specifically is kept. What would settle it: verify no caller-supplied count field exists in _ALLOWED_PARTICIPANT_KEYS (not in this chunk).

verify_chain | medium | Docstring claims 'Three independent checks per line' but the body_sha check uses _body_sha(rec) which may depend on the same fields that _entry_sha uses; independence is not fully demonstrable in this chunk. What would settle it: inspect _body_sha and _entry_sha implementations.

load_transcript | low | Docstring says 'skipping a torn tail line (never fatal)' but the code skips ANY unparseable line, not just the tail; could mask mid-file corruption. What would settle it: confirm intent from tests or other docs.

transcript_head | low | Docstring says 'the tail anchor, recomputed from the file' but the code returns the last record's entry_sha from a JSON load, not from the anchor file; the phrase 'tail anchor' could be misleading. What would settle it: confirm terminology in other docs.

verify_chain | low | When store_path is missing and expected_count/expected_head are None, the function returns (True, []) — but the docstring says 'compare against read_anchor to catch a truncation'; the default behavior with no anchor is to treat missing file as OK, which may be surprising. What would settle it: check call sites.

verify_chain | low | The docstring says 'a valid chain's prefix is a valid chain' — the code does not actually verify that a prefix is valid; it only checks the tail via anchor. The claim is explanatory, not a behavioral promise, but could be misread. What would settle it: no action.

append_roster | low | The docstring says 'a consumer that shows the participant count instead of the distinct-class count is showing a council of clones as a council' — this is a design rationale, not a checkable behavior in this chunk. What would settle it: no action.

handoff.purpose: Public append/read/verify API for the council transcript chain: append_round, append_turn, append_roster, load_transcript, transcript_head, read_anchor, verify_chain.

symbols.name: append_round
symbols.note: Chains a whole round; normalizes, scans, refuses, sorts, chains. Raises ValueError on empty turns or duplicate actors (except council.redacted.redacted).

symbols.name: append_turn
symbols.note: Convenience wrapper calling append_round with a single turn; returns first id.

symbols.name: append_roster
symbols.note: Chains a roster record; validates phase, actor format, outcome; derives counts and distinct_classes; can emit a refused variant.

symbols.name: load_transcript
symbols.note: Reads all JSON lines, skipping blank and unparseable lines; returns [] if file missing.

symbols.name: transcript_head
symbols.note: Returns (record_count, last entry_sha) or (0, None) if empty.

symbols.name: read_anchor
symbols.note: Reads the anchor JSON file; returns None if missing or unparseable.

symbols.name: verify_chain
symbols.note: Walks the chain, checks body_sha, entry_sha, prev linkage; optionally checks count/head against anchor or explicit expectations.

claims.text: Turns are normalised, secret-floored, then sorted by actor id and chained with ``seq`` assigned here -- so reversed completion order yields a byte-identical chain head.
claims.why: This chunk shows the sort and the call to _chain_records, but the normalisation and secret-flooring happen in _normalize_turn and _scan_turn, which are not in this chunk. The claim about byte-identical chain head depends on those helpers.

claims.text: Exactly one turn per actor per round is allowed: a duplicate is a caller bug that would double a voice, and a missing participant must be recorded as an ``unavailable`` turn rather than skipped.
claims.why: Lines 569-574 (within this chunk) detect duplicates (excluding 'council.redacted.redacted') and raise ValueError. The 'unavailable' requirement is not enforced here but is stated as caller responsibility; the duplicate check is present.

claims.text: a round with no turns is not a round: every requested participant produces exactly one chained turn
claims.why: Lines 561-563 raise ValueError if turns is empty.

claims.text: REFUSE. The offending bytes never reach the file -- not in the turn, and not in the receipt.
claims.why: Lines 566-571: if _scan_turn returns a rule, the receipt replaces rec, and the receipt is re-scanned; if it still has a rule, an anonymous variant is used. The original turn is not appended; only the receipt is.

claims.text: Canonical body is the final tiebreak so the order is TOTAL even when two anonymised refusal receipts collapse to the same actor: chaining must not inherit wall-clock completion order from anywhere.
claims.why: Lines 575-577 sort by (actor, role, status, canonical_body_json(r)). canonical_body_json is not defined in this chunk but is imported/defined elsewhere; the sort key is as claimed.

claims.text: Chain a single turn (a one-participant round). Convenience over :func:`append_round`; prefer the round form so ordering stays deterministic.
claims.why: Lines 579-582 call append_round with a single-element list and return the first id.

claims.text: Chain the roster accounting: requested / seated / responded / unavailable with machine reasons, plus the DISTINCT INDEPENDENCE CLASS count and a ``degraded`` flag whenever fewer participants responded than were requested.
claims.why: Lines 604-617 compute requested, seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes, and degraded = responded < requested.

claims.text: Counts are DERIVED here, never accepted from the caller: "3 of 4" and "2 of 2" must not be able to render as the same string, and a consumer that shows the participant count instead of the distinct-class count is showing a council of clones as a council.
claims.why: Counts are computed from the normalized participant list (lines 604-617); no count field is read from the input dicts. The distinct_classes uses a set of heard_classes, so duplicates are collapsed.

claims.text: Duplicate weights are detected over everyone SEATED (that is when the clone was let in); the distinct-class count is over those who actually RESPONDED, because an unavailable participant contributes no voice and a class count that includes it overstates the independence on the record.
claims.why: Lines 592-601: seated_classes includes outcomes 'seated', 'responded', 'refused'; heard_classes only 'responded'. dup is computed over seated_classes; distinct_classes over heard_classes.

claims.text: Availability is not correctness: a council that lost a voice says so.
Read all records, skipping a torn tail line (never fatal). Missing is [].
claims.why: Lines 629-639: if file missing returns []; reads text with errors='replace'; skips blank lines; on JSONDecodeError continues. It skips any unparseable line, not just the tail, but the claim 'skipping a torn tail line' is a subset; the 'never fatal' and 'Missing is []' are kept.

claims.text: ``(record_count, head_entry_sha)`` -- the tail anchor, recomputed from the file. Compare against :func:`read_anchor` to catch a truncation.
claims.why: Lines 641-644: returns len(records) and the last record's entry_sha (or None). The 'tail anchor' terminology is loose but the behavior is as described: it recomputes from the file.

claims.text: Walk the chain; return ``(ok, failures)`` where every failure NAMES the 1-indexed line and what mismatched. Never a bare False.
claims.why: Lines 651-694: failures list contains strings with line numbers and reasons; returns (not failures, failures).

claims.text: Three independent checks per line: * ``body_sha`` recomputed over the canonical body -- catches a content edit; * ``entry_sha`` recomputed over ``(prev, stored body_sha, ts)`` -- catches a back-dated ts or a rewritten link where body_sha WAS updated; * ``prev`` equals the previous line's ``entry_sha`` -- catches a deleted or reordered line (the survivor points at a vanished predecessor).
claims.why: Lines 680-690: body_sha check via _body_sha(rec) != stored_body; entry_sha check via _entry_sha(rec.get('prev'), stored_body or '', rec.get('ts','')) != stored_entry; prev check via rec.get('prev') != prev_entry_sha. The independence is not fully provable here but the three checks are present.

claims.text: TAIL truncation is the one deletion a per-line walk cannot catch (a valid chain's prefix is a valid chain), so the persisted anchor is consulted by default and a shortfall in count or head is NAMED. Explicit ``expected_count`` / ``expected_head`` override it; ``use_anchor=False`` verifies linkage only.
claims.why: Lines 665-670: if use_anchor and no explicit expectations, reads anchor and sets expected_count/expected_head. Lines 691-694: count and head mismatches are appended. use_anchor=False skips that block.

claims.text: Cannot advance prev to a sha we do not have; leave it so the next line also flags rather than silently re-syncing.
claims.why: Lines 676-679: on JSONDecodeError, prev_entry_sha is not updated, so the next line will also flag a prev mismatch.

observations.what: append_round docstring says 'Turns are normalised, secret-floored, then sorted' but this chunk only shows the sort and the call to _chain_records; the normalisation and secret-flooring are in _normalize_turn and _scan_turn which are not in this chunk.

append_roster docstring claims counts are derived and never accepted from caller, but the participant dicts themselves are caller-supplied and fields like vendor/model are derived with fallbacks; the count claim is kept but the broader 'never accepted' is only about counts.

verify_chain docstring claims 'Three independent checks per line' but the body_sha check uses _body_sha(rec) which may depend on the same fields that _entry_sha uses; independence is not fully demonstrable in this chunk.
load_transcript skips any unparseable line, not just the tail; the docstring says 'skipping a torn tail line' which could understate the behavior.

transcript_head calls the last entry_sha 'the tail anchor' but it is not read from the anchor file; the docstring says 'recomputed from the file' which is accurate but 'tail anchor' is loose terminology.

verify_chain when store_path is missing and no expectations are set returns (True, []) — the docstring says 'compare against read_anchor to catch a truncation' but with no anchor and no expectations, a missing file passes.

The docstring in verify_chain says 'a valid chain's prefix is a valid chain' but the code does not actually verify prefixes; it only checks the tail via anchor. This is an explanatory comment, not a behavioral promise, but could be misread.
